newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says Arafat ready to renew security ties.
newsitem.headline: Israel says Arafat ready to renew security ties.

text.p: Israel's Foreign Minister David Levy said on Wednesday he had secured a promise from Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat during a meeting in Malta to renew security cooperation with the Jewish state.
"He (Arafat) announced that the cooperation on security matters will be renewed," Levy told reporters in remarks monitored by Reuters in Jerusalem.

Palestinian officials were not immediately available for comment on the issue. Arafat's spokesman Marwan Kanafani said in Malta that the two sides had recommitted themselves to the peace process but "no substance was discussed".
In Jerusalem, U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross was due to meet Israel's leader Benjamin Netanyahu and Arafat separately later on Wednesday in a bid to revive peacemaking.
The PLO cut off security contacts last month after Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Since then, Palestinian stone-throwers have battled Israeli troops in the West Bank almost daily. A Palestinian bomber killed three Israeli women at a Tel Aviv cafe.

Arafat had said earlier he would renew security cooperation only after Israel agreed to freeze the settlement plan. His meeting with Levy on Wednesday was the first high-level contact since the crisis in peacemaking began.
But Palestinian officials said the only way out of the crisis is for Israel to pull its bulldozers off the hill in East Jerusalem.

"If Dennis Ross comes tonight with ideas that do not include halting the Israeli unilateral actions, this means he is coming to save Netanyahu and not the peace process," Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat told Reuters.

Palestinians say Israeli settlement construction in East Jerusalem violates peace deals and international law. Israel claims all of Jerusalem as its capital and says it has the right to build anywhere in the city.
